```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ringtest) # remotes::install_github("bserrien/ringtest")
```


```{r}
#| label: import-data

load(here("data/ringtest-pilot.rda"))

# choose substrate of interest
data_ringtest_subst <- data_ringtest |> 
  filter(subst == "Benzo[a]anthracene") |> 
  unnest(cols = data)

```


## Data inspection

Are there any labs with more than 1 record? 
No

```{r}
data_ringtest_subst |> 
  filter(.by = lab_code, n() > 1) |> 
  select(lab_code, meas_1, meas_2, meas_3, meas_mean)
data_ringtest_subst_clean <- data_ringtest_subst
```

Are all measurements in the same units?
Yes.

```{r}
unique(data_ringtest_subst_clean$meas_unit)
```

Do all labs report in the same way? 
No

```{r}
data_ringtest_subst_clean |> 
  summarise(.by = data_status, N = n())
```

A minimum reporting requirement for a lab should be:

- 3 replicate measurements
- measurement mean and uncertainty (SD)

The following labs don't meet the criteria:

```{r}
data_ringtest_subst_clean <- data_ringtest_subst_clean |> 
  mutate(
    check = case_when(
      !is.na(meas_1) & !is.na(meas_2) & !is.na(meas_3) ~ "3 measures",
      !is.na(meas_mean) & !is.na(meas_uncertain) ~ "mean +/- SD",
      TRUE ~ "not OK"
    )
  )

data_ringtest_subst_clean |> 
  filter(check == "not OK") |> 
  select(lab_code, meas_1, meas_2, meas_3, meas_4, meas_5, 
         meas_mean, meas_uncertain)

data_ringtest_subst_clean <- data_ringtest_subst_clean |> 
  filter(check != "not OK")
```

We remove the labs not meeting the above requirements (ISO clause 8.4.3.a).
The alternative is clause 8.4.3.b but I favor to have the same set of labs; to be discussed.

In @fig-vizraw we display the data after the above cleaning steps.

```{r}
#| label: fig-vizraw
#| fig-cap: "Raw data vizualisation. For labs reporting at least 3 measures we show the individual measurements and an error-bar extending to +/- 1 SD. For the labs reporting only the mean +/- SD, we show the mean and error-bar only."

# standard value (reference measurement?)
standard    <- unique(data_ringtest_subst_clean$standard_total_value)
standard_sd <- unique(data_ringtest_subst_clean$standard_total_uncertain)

data_labs_ind <- data_ringtest_subst_clean |>
  filter(check == "3 measures") |> 
  select(lab_code, contains("meas_")) |> 
  select(-meas_unit) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    paste0("meas_", 1:5), names_to = "replicate", 
    values_to = "soil_descriptor"
  ) |> 
  filter(!is.na(soil_descriptor)) |> 
  mutate(
    .by = lab_code, 
    meas_mean      = mean(soil_descriptor),
    meas_uncertain = sd(soil_descriptor)
  )

data_labs_aggr <- data_ringtest_subst_clean |>
  filter(check == "mean +/- SD") |> 
  select(lab_code, meas_mean, meas_uncertain)

ggplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = standard, lty = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = standard + c(-1, 1) * standard_sd, lty = 3) +
  geom_point(
    data = data_labs_ind, 
    aes(lab_code, soil_descriptor, color = "at least 3 measures")
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = data_labs_ind, 
    aes(lab_code, color = "at least 3 measures", 
        ymin = meas_mean - meas_uncertain,
        ymax = meas_mean + meas_uncertain)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = data_labs_aggr, 
    aes(lab_code, meas_mean, color = "mean +/- SD")
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = data_labs_aggr, 
    aes(lab_code, color = "mean +/- SD",
        ymin = meas_mean - meas_uncertain,
        ymax = meas_mean + meas_uncertain)
  ) +
  labs(x = "lab", y = "soil descriptor", color = "type of reporting",
       caption = "The horizontal dashed lines are the standard mean +/- standard SD")

```

## Proficiency test (ISO procedure)

How should we deal with this difference in reporting? 
We can't use REML estimation, as this requires the raw data per replicate for all labs.
We therefore use the classic approach based on cell-statistics.

We combine the cell-statistics from the two types of reporting.
For labs reporting aggregated data, it is not reported on how many replicates this is based; we make the assumption of three replicates, but this needs verification.

```{r}
cell_stats <- rbind(
  # labs reporting individual data 
  data_labs_ind |> 
    rename(
      lab = lab_code,
      value = soil_descriptor
    ) |> 
    mutate(level = 1) |> 
    calc_cell_stats(),
  # labs reporting aggregated data
  data_labs_aggr |> 
    rename(
      lab = lab_code,
      mean = meas_mean,
      sd = meas_uncertain
    ) |> 
    mutate(
      level = 1, 
      n = 3 # assumption: it is not reported on how many replicates it is based
    )
)

print(cell_stats)
```

We calculate the Mandel $h$ and $k$ statistics to inspect for outlying means and variances, results are shown in @fig-mandel.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mandel
#| fig-cap: "Mandel's h & k statistics. Labs with outlying values at the 5% significance level are colored differently."

calc_mandel_hk(cell_stats, alpha = 0.05) |> 
  plot_mandel_hk()
```

Outlier removal should be an interactive process where the experts from the panel evaluate the data from a lab that is identified as outlier or straggler.
For now I just follow the statistical ISO procedure where I retain stragglers and remove outliers.
The ISO procedure mentions that only 2/9 of the data from a given level should be removed (8.3.6.2§2); which means for `r nrow(cell_stats)` labs only `r round((2/9) * nrow(cell_stats))` can be removed; however, we previously removed already labs not meeting the reporting requirements, and I'm not sure if we have to count them as well?
The final cleaned statistics per lab are shown in @fig-clean-cellstats.

```{r}
# iteration (1)
outl_strag_1 <- cell_stats |> 
  test_outliers() |> 
  filter(!is.na(coalesce(cochran, grubbs_single, grubbs_double)))
outl_strag_1
outl_1 <- outl_strag_1 |> 
  filter(
    cochran == "Outlier (**)" | 
      grubbs_single == "Outlier (**)" |
      grubbs_double == "Outlier (**)"
  )
cell_stats_1 <- anti_join(cell_stats, outl_1, by = c("lab", "level"))

# iteration (2)
outl_strag_2 <- cell_stats_1 |> 
  test_outliers() |> 
  filter(!is.na(coalesce(cochran, grubbs_single, grubbs_double)))
outl_strag_2
outl_2 <- outl_strag_2 |> 
  filter(
    cochran == "Outlier (**)" | 
      grubbs_single == "Outlier (**)" |
      grubbs_double == "Outlier (**)"
  )
cell_stats_2 <- anti_join(cell_stats_1, outl_2, by = c("lab", "level"))

# iteration (3)
outl_strag_3 <- cell_stats_2 |> 
  test_outliers() |> 
  filter(!is.na(coalesce(cochran, grubbs_single, grubbs_double)))
outl_strag_3 # => no outliers/stragglers are identified, the procedure ends

cell_stats_final <- cell_stats_2
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-clean-cellstats
#| fig-cap: "Aggregated statistics per lab after outlier removal."

cell_stats_final |> 
  ggplot(aes(lab, mean, ymin = mean - sd, ymax = mean + sd)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar() +
  labs(x = "lab", y = "soil descriptor")
```

We now calculate the cleand mean and the variance components (as SD):

- `m_hat` = cleaned mean
- `s_r` = repeatability SD
- `s_L` = inter-laboratory SD
- `s_R` = reproducibility SD

$$
\sigma_R^2 = \sigma_r^2 + \sigma_L^2
$$

```{r}
res <- ringtest(cell_stats_final)
res
```

The reported standard measures (`standard_total_value` and `standard_total_uncertainty`) are shown below for comparison.
How are these values defined/calculated? (otherwise difficult to compare with results of the ringtest)

```{r}
data_ringtest_subst_clean |> 
  distinct(standard_total_value, standard_total_uncertain)
```
